chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the Sa'i (circumambulation) between As-Safa and Al-Marwah while riding a beast. He said, 'Yes, and while riding a mount.'

key_terms.اَلدَّابَّةِ: Ad-dabbah: A beast of burden or riding animal
key_terms.اَلسَّعْيِ: Sa'i: The ritual walking or running between the hills of Safa and Marwah
key_terms.اَلصَّفَا: As-Safa: One of the two hills between which Sa'i is performed
key_terms.اَلْمَحْمِلِ: Al-mahmal: A mount or saddle animal
key_terms.اَلْمَرْوَةِ: Al-Marwah: The second hill between which Sa'i is performed

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform Sa'i between Safa and Marwah while riding a horse or camel?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the flexibility of the Sa'i ritual by permitting pilgrims to perform it while riding a mount or being carried in a litter (mahmal). This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle of ease (taysir) in worship, accommodating those with physical limitations or specific needs during the pilgrimage rites between Safa and Marwa.
